questions.q: What is Fixed Assets period close?
options: A single button that instantly finalizes a period
A report listing retired assets
A one-time setup task performed only at implementation
A sequence of dependent steps moving a book's current period from open to final
questions.explain: Period close is a multi-step sequence — transaction entry, depreciation, accounting, GL transfer, and reconciliation — not a single action.

questions.q: Which step in the close sequence actually closes the current period in the depreciation calendar?
options: Running depreciation in preview mode
Running depreciation in final mode
Transferring to the General Ledger
Reconciliation
questions.explain: Final mode depreciation commits the period's calculated depreciation and is the step that actually advances the book's current open period.

questions.q: Why can't the Fixed Assets to GL transfer happen before Create Accounting runs?
options: It can happen before, with no issue
Because GL transfer always happens automatically regardless of order
Because transfer only applies to tax books
Because there are no journal entries yet to transfer until Create Accounting generates them
questions.explain: Create Accounting generates the journal entries; without that step having run, there's nothing yet for the GL transfer to move.

questions.q: What blocks a period from closing, as established in earlier lessons?
options: A category with too many minor segments
An asset placed in service mid-month
A tax book with a different life than the corporate book
Assets that have failed to depreciate
questions.explain: A period generally cannot close while any assets have failed to depreciate, which is why reviewing the preview exception report is a critical step before final depreciation.

questions.q: Why is a messy period close (full of exceptions, reconciliation not tying out) usually a symptom rather than the actual root problem?
options: Because period close causes problems that didn't exist before
Because period close is unrelated to any earlier chapter's work
Because messy closes are purely random and have no underlying cause
Because close surfaces issues from earlier steps — setup, additions, adjustments — all at the one moment they can no longer be ignored
questions.explain: A clean close reflects correct setup and discipline throughout the asset lifecycle; a messy close usually traces back to a problem introduced earlier that surfaces at close.
